{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.",
    "If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or volatility, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to account for mean reversion.",
    "After a recent price spike, model often overcorrects downward; if sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast decline rate by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.",
    "When sentiment history shows multiple 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 2–5% to reflect latent bullish bias.",
    "If true outcome deviates significantly from forecast in first 5–7 days (e.g., >5% drop), model is lagging; adjust forecast to match recent history’s volatility pattern.",
    "If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows rapid rise, model underestimates momentum; increase forecast slope by 1–3% if sentiment is positive.",
    "If sentiment history includes 0.40 or higher, model often overestimates downside risk; reduce forecast decline by 5–10% to avoid pessimism bias."
  ]
}
